## 1. One-paragraph verdict
A genuine, structurally perfect, truthfully-named fixture. My IVF walk
consumed all 512 bytes: header (version 0, hdrlen 32, AV01, 192×108,
rate 6/scale 1, frame count 6) + exactly 6 frame records with pts 0..5
and the size profile of a static pattern (288-byte keyframe + five ~23-26
byte inter frames — a still image, matching rgbtestsrc). ffprobe agrees:
av1 Main profile, 192×108, yuv420p, nb_frames=6. The "rgb" name claim I
verified at the pixel level: ffmpeg's rgb24 decode of frame 0 shows
exactly the rgbtestsrc pattern — three stacked horizontal bands, red ramp
(R 1→250 L-to-R), green ramp (G 2→250), blue ramp (B 5→248). The fixture
is one of the three 8-bit bit-exact differential lanes (Truth row at
av1_differential.rs:76-80: frames 6, (192,108), yuv_md5
f153f1d34f1c8828a8c061fefc100d74 — matching the recorded
worklog:9560 / video-av1.md:232-243 evidence chain), and it is the
suite's workhorse beyond the lane table: the fuzz-lite test mutates its
TU for 3000 structure-aware rounds (:563) and the error-path test uses it
as the post-damage clean-recovery probe (:391). I executed the whole
suite live: 6/6 passed in 9.29s — frame-count/dims/pts vs ffprobe, pixel
MD5 vs the live ffmpeg dump, corruption resync, tenbit typed refusal,
fuzz survival.
